title: Vanishing of first cohomology for ideal twists implies ampleness
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent] there exists an integer $n\ge1$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=0$, with cohomology as in [pqf-def-cohomology] and tensor product and powers as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $\mathcal L$ is ample in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

proof.text: Since f is proper and Spec(R) is affine, the proper-basic lemma makes X quasi-compact. We will construct affine nonvanishing neighbourhoods for every closed point, then show that their union is X.

source.place: Tag 0B5U, lemma-vanshing-gives-ample (3) => (1), and Tag 0B5P, lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-invertible, hypothesis (1).

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in X$. The common-free-generator lemma, with both modules equal to $\mathcal L$ and $W=X$, gives an affine neighbourhood $U$ and a generator $e$. Apply the twisted-ideal-quotient lemma to obtain the reduced ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$, their quotient $\mathcal Q$, the exact tensor sequences and injective maps for every positive power, and the quotient sections $q_n$ with nonzero residue at $x$. In particular $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent.

Apply the hypothesis to the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J$ of step 2, choosing $n\ge1$ with $H^1(X,\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=0$. In the supported-section lifting lemma take $\mathcal M=\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$, $a=e^{\otimes n}$, $q=q_n$, and the same $\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\mathcal Q$ and canonical maps as step 2. The ampleness-definition node gives invertibility of this tensor power; on $U$ its generator is $e^{\otimes n}$. Step 2 gives $\mathcal J_x=\mathfrak m_x\subseteq\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the exact tensor sequence, injectivity into $\mathcal M$, and the canonical nonzero quotient germ. The chosen vanishing is precisely the remaining lifting hypothesis. Its conclusion supplies $t$ and its image $s$ with $x\in X_s=U_f$ affine. This construction applies to every closed point $x$.

Let W be the union of X_s over all positive powers and sections whose nonvanishing open is affine. Each X_s is open by the ampleness-definition node, and steps 2--3 show that W contains every closed point. The underlying space of X is Kolmogorov: if two points had the same closure, that irreducible closed subset would have two generic points, contrary to the scheme-sobriety lemma; distinct closures are distinguished by an open complement. Apply the quasi-compact Kolmogorov closed-point lemma to the closed subset X minus W of the quasi-compact space X. If nonempty, it contains a point closed in X, contradicting that all closed points lie in W. Hence W=X.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, final paragraph, the closed-point covering argument; the cited closed-point lemma applies directly to a closed subset of X.

proof.text: X is quasi-compact by step 1. The equality W=X gives, for every point of X, a positive power of L and a section of that power with affine nonvanishing locus containing the point. These are precisely the two clauses of absolute ampleness. Therefore L is ample.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B5U, lemma-vanshing-gives-ample (3) => (1), expanded by the full proof of Tag 0B5P, lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-invertible.
